items.t: Drive unit grinding or milling noise
items.job: Replace drive unit with a remanufactured unit
items.note: Owners report about $8,000 out of warranty; Tesla once quoted much more. Minor noises are sometimes fixed with a shim or by securing a loose cable for far less.

items.t: Door handles won't extend or open the door
items.job: Repair or replace one door handle assembly
items.note: Owners report $168–$535 per handle. Rebuilding with a new gear or harness is the cheaper route.

items.t: Touchscreen goes blank from worn memory chip (recall 21V-035)
items.job: Recall repair or software update at Tesla
items.note: Free under the recall. Enter your VIN on Tesla's or NHTSA's recall lookup to check.

items.t: Yellow border or bubbles on the screens
items.job: Replace center display or upgrade to MCU2
items.note: Owners report about $1,100–$1,800, including MCU2 upgrades.

items.t: Battery coolant heater fails
items.job: Replace battery coolant heater
items.note: Owners report about $800–$1,250.

items.t: Onboard charger stops charging
items.job: Replace onboard charger
items.note: Owners report about $1,700–$2,300.

items.t: DC-DC converter failure
items.job: Replace DC-DC converter
items.note: Owners report about $1,800–$2,250.

items.t: Air suspension sags or fails
items.job: Replace one air strut (with compressor if failed)
items.note: One corner is the typical repair; a full system at Tesla has been quoted up to $14,000. Aftermarket coil-over kits cost about $2,000 in parts.

items.t: Front control arms and links clunk
items.job: Replace worn control arms and align
items.note: Owners report $300 for a single arm and $1,100–$2,700 for pairs or several links.

items.t: 12-volt battery dies early
items.job: Replace 12-volt battery
items.note: Owners usually pay $100–$300.

items.t: Parking brake caliper seizes
items.job: Replace parking brake caliper
items.note: Owners report about $200–$600.

items.t: Wind noise from doors and windows
items.job: Adjust door and window alignment, replace seals
items.note: Seal adjustments are cheap; one owner paid $1,700 to realign a sagging door.

items.t: Charge port door or latch faults
items.job: Repair charge port door motor, sensor or wiring
items.note: Owners report about $95–$125 for a sensor or wiring repair; a full charge port costs more.

items.t: Headlight LED or daytime light failure
items.job: Replace headlight assembly
items.note: Owners report about $900–$1,250 (Canadian) per side.

items.t: Tire pressure monitor errors
items.job: Replace tire pressure sensor or upgrade the system
items.note: About $127 for one sensor; $1,200–$1,375 to upgrade sensors and receiver.
